walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme 4: A Global Perspective — a core area of A-Level Economics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme 4: A Global Perspective brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme 4: A Global Perspective.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is asymmetric information as a source of market failure?
options: Automatic stabilisers are special government emergency funds.
Asymmetric information is when a market only operates in one direction.
Asymmetric information means a buyer and seller disagree about a price.

When one party in a transaction knows more than the other — leading to problems like adverse selection (used-car market) or moral hazard (insurance). Markets can fail or unravel when information is unequal.
Automatic stabilisers are special government emergency funds.

Features of the tax and benefit system that automatically cushion the economy without new legislation — e.g. unemployment benefits rise in slumps; tax revenues fall as incomes fall, supporting demand.
Asymmetric information is when a market only operates in one direction.
Automatic stabilisers are interest rate changes by the central bank.
